name: guee

attributes.attribute: A Manx term for a curse or prayer.
On the Isle of Man people both prayed and cursed while kneeling.
Skeab Lome means naked broom in Manx.
The curse invoked a broom to sweep away evil.

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: On the Isle of Man, people traditionally offered both prayers and curses while kneeling. They called this act of cursing wishing upon the knees. A strong traditional curse was the Skeab Lome, or naked broom. The curse invoked a broom as a power to sweep away evil and one's enemies.

okr.objective: Describe the Manx practice of guee, prayer and cursing performed while kneeling.
key_results: Isle of Man tradition mixed prayer and cursing while kneeling
Cursing was called wishing upon the knees
The Skeab Lome or naked broom was a strong traditional curse
A broom was invoked to sweep away evil
